title: ⁴√2 has degree 4 over ℚ: X⁴ − 2 irreducible via Eisenstein + Gauss, [ℚ(⁴√2):ℚ] = 4
description: The fourth root of 2 is irrational, and more sharply has degree exactly 4 over ℚ. We prove X⁴ − 2 is irreducible over ℚ — the case 4 = 2² that Mathlib's Kummer-theory API explicitly cannot handle (its irreducibility lemmas require an odd exponent / prime p ≠ 2) — by Eisenstein's criterion at 2 over ℤ followed by Gauss's lemma. This identifies the minimal polynomial of ⁴√2, gives [ℚ(⁴√2):ℚ] = 4, the quadratic tower ℚ ⊂ ℚ(√2) ⊂ ℚ(⁴√2), and the ℚ-linear independence of the power basis {1, ⁴√2, √2, ⁴√8}.
overview:
This entry establishes the full algebraic structure of the real fourth root of 2 (modeled as √√2), going well beyond bare irrationality.

The arithmetic seed is `no_rat_fourth_two`: 2 has no rational fourth root (if q⁴ = 2 then q² is a rational square root of 2, contradicting the irrationality of √2). From this, `fr2_irrational` recovers ⁴√2 ∉ ℚ.

The heart of the entry is the irreducibility of **X⁴ − 2 over ℚ**. This is exactly the case Mathlib's Kummer-extension API cannot reach: `X_pow_sub_C_irreducible_of_prime_pow` requires the prime p ≠ 2, and `X_pow_sub_C_irreducible_of_odd` requires an odd exponent — and the source carries explicit `TODO: generalize to p = 2 / even n` comments. Since 4 = 2², neither applies. We instead route through **Eisenstein's criterion at the prime 2** over ℤ (the lower coefficients 0, 0, 0, −2 all lie in the ideal (2), the constant term −2 avoids (2)² = (4), and the leading coefficient 1 avoids (2)), via Mathlib's `irreducible_of_eisenstein_criterion`, and then descend to ℚ by **Gauss's lemma** (`IsPrimitive.Int.irreducible_iff_irreducible_map_cast`).

Monicity plus (⁴√2)⁴ = 2 then identify X⁴ − 2 as the **minimal polynomial** of ⁴√2 (`minpoly_fr2`), the simple-extension dimension formula gives **[ℚ(⁴√2):ℚ] = 4** (`finrank_adjoin_fr2`), and `linearIndependent_pow` yields the **ℚ-linear independence of {1, ⁴√2, (⁴√2)², (⁴√2)³} = {1, ⁴√2, √2, ⁴√8}**. We also exhibit the bottom of the quadratic tower: √2 = (⁴√2)² ∈ ℚ(⁴√2) and [ℚ(√2):ℚ] = 2, so the degrees multiply as 4 = 2 · 2.
conclusion: X⁴ − 2 is irreducible over ℚ and is the minimal polynomial of ⁴√2, so [ℚ(⁴√2):ℚ] = 4, the power basis {1, ⁴√2, √2, ⁴√8} is ℚ-linearly independent, and ℚ ⊂ ℚ(√2) ⊂ ℚ(⁴√2) is a tower of quadratic extensions. All sixteen results are fully machine-checked with no sorries and no axioms beyond Lean/Mathlib's foundational propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound (no native_decide). Notably, the degree-4 irreducibility is obtained for the 2-power exponent that Mathlib's dedicated X^n − C irreducibility lemmas explicitly exclude.

originalContributions: no_rat_fourth_two: 2 has no rational fourth root, derived from the irrationality of √2 (if q⁴ = 2 then q² is a rational √2). The single arithmetic input for irrationality.

irreducible_X4_sub_2_int: X⁴ − 2 is irreducible over ℤ via Eisenstein's criterion at the prime 2 (Polynomial.irreducible_of_eisenstein_criterion with P = (2): leading coeff 1 ∉ (2), lower coeffs ∈ (2), constant term −2 ∉ (2)² = (4)).

irreducible_X4_sub_2_rat: X⁴ − 2 is irreducible over ℚ, by Gauss's lemma descending irreducibility of the primitive integer polynomial. This is the 4 = 2² case that Mathlib's X_pow_sub_C_irreducible_of_prime_pow / _of_odd lemmas explicitly exclude (they require p ≠ 2 / odd exponent).
minpoly_fr2: X⁴ − 2 is the minimal polynomial of ⁴√2 over ℚ.
finrank_adjoin_fr2: the field extension degree [ℚ(⁴√2) : ℚ] = Module.finrank ℚ ℚ⟮fr2⟯ = 4.
sqrt2_mem_adjoin_fr2 + finrank_adjoin_sqrt2: the quadratic tower ℚ ⊂ ℚ(√2) ⊂ ℚ(⁴√2) — √2 = (⁴√2)² lies in ℚ(⁴√2), and [ℚ(√2):ℚ] = 2 (X² − 2 irreducible), so 4 = 2 · 2.

linearIndependent_fr2_powers: the power basis {1, ⁴√2, (⁴√2)², (⁴√2)³} = {1, ⁴√2, √2, ⁴√8} is ℚ-linearly independent (Fin 4 LinearIndependent predicate form), via linearIndependent_pow at the minimal-polynomial degree.
fr2_no_cubic_relation: ⁴√2 satisfies no rational relation of degree ≤ 3 — the explicit elementary reading of the linear independence.

sections.title: The arithmetic input: 2 has no rational fourth root
sections.content: no_rat_fourth_two shows q⁴ ≠ 2 for all q ∈ ℚ. If q⁴ = 2, then r := q² satisfies (r:ℝ)² = 2 with r ≥ 0, so √2 = r is rational — contradicting irrational_sqrt_two. This gives fr2_irrational (⁴√2 ∉ ℚ).

sections.title: Irreducibility of X⁴ − 2: Eisenstein at 2, then Gauss
sections.content: The dedicated Mathlib lemmas X_pow_sub_C_irreducible_of_prime_pow and _of_odd require p ≠ 2 / odd exponent, so they miss 4 = 2². Instead, over ℤ we apply Polynomial.irreducible_of_eisenstein_criterion with the prime ideal P = (2): the leading coefficient 1 ∉ (2), every lower coefficient (0, 0, 0, −2) lies in (2), and the constant term −2 ∉ (2)² = (4). This yields irreducibility over ℤ; Gauss's lemma (IsPrimitive.Int.irreducible_iff_irreducible_map_cast) then descends it to ℚ.

sections.title: Minimal polynomial and field degree
sections.content: Since ⁴√2 is a root of the monic irreducible X⁴ − 2, minpoly.eq_of_irreducible_of_monic gives minpoly ℚ (⁴√2) = X⁴ − 2. The simple-extension dimension formula IntermediateField.adjoin.finrank then gives [ℚ(⁴√2) : ℚ] = natDegree(X⁴ − 2) = 4.

sections.title: The quadratic tower and the power basis
sections.content: Because (⁴√2)² = √2, we have √2 ∈ ℚ(⁴√2), and [ℚ(√2):ℚ] = 2 (X² − 2 is irreducible since √2 ∉ ℚ), exhibiting the tower ℚ ⊂ ℚ(√2) ⊂ ℚ(⁴√2) with 4 = 2 · 2. Finally, linearIndependent_pow at the minimal-polynomial degree shows {1, ⁴√2, √2, ⁴√8} is ℚ-linearly independent; fr2_no_cubic_relation restates this as the absence of any rational degree-≤3 relation.
